title: Semantic layer: add unit economics views w/ stable columns + join docs; deprecate ad-hoc queries
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Internal-only: adds curated semantic views for unit economics (daily + hourly aggregates) with stable column names and documented joins; marks legacy ad-hoc unit-econ queries as deprecated.
description:
Context
This PR introduces a small semantic layer for the internal unit economics dashboard so Product/Finance/Eng can query consistent, versioned datasets without relying on ad-hoc SQL. The goal is to make $/1M output tokens drilldowns reproducible and compatible with reconciliation.

What’s in this PR
- Adds curated semantic views for unit economics with stable column names and explicit grain:
  - semantic.unit_econ_daily (1 row per day x model_variant x region x customer_tier [+ optional runtime_config/quantization_profile when present])
  - semantic.unit_econ_hourly (hourly partitions for faster debugging + freshness monitoring)
  - semantic.unit_econ_driver_daily (pre-aggregated driver components used in the “Explain” panel: compute_cost_usd, overhead_cost_usd_allocated, cache_savings_usd_est, credits_usd_applied, discounts_usd_applied)
- Documents join keys and mapping tables (model catalog, region normalization, tier mapping), including allowed filter dimensions to keep cardinality bounded.
- Deprecates older ad-hoc datasets by:
  - moving legacy views under adhoc_deprecated.*
  - adding comments + ownership pointers + “do not use for dashboard” warnings
  - updating internal references in scheduled jobs and notebooks used by Console/BI.

Metric contract notes
- All cost fields are in USD, aggregated at the view grain.
- Canonical headline metric:
  - blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd = (compute_cost_usd + overhead_cost_usd_allocated - cache_savings_usd_est + credits_usd_applied + discounts_usd_applied) / (output_tokens / 1,000,000)
- output_tokens and input_tokens are included for context; the KPI denominates on output_tokens per ADR.
- customer_tier uses the new tier mapping table (historically correct; effective_start/end).

Schema (semantic.unit_econ_daily)
- dt (DATE)
- model_family (STRING)
- model_variant (STRING)
- model_version (STRING)
- region (STRING)  -- normalized (e.g., us-east, us-west, eu-west)
- customer_tier (STRING)  -- self_serve | dedicated | private | enterprise
- runtime_config (STRING)  -- optional, NULL-safe; capped set (see docs)
- quantization_profile (STRING)  -- optional, NULL-safe
- requests (BIGINT)
- output_tokens (BIGINT)
- input_tokens (BIGINT)
- compute_cost_usd (DOUBLE)
- overhead_cost_usd_allocated (DOUBLE)
- cache_savings_usd_est (DOUBLE)
- credits_usd_applied (DOUBLE)
- discounts_usd_applied (DOUBLE)
- blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd (DOUBLE)
- data_completeness_ratio (DOUBLE)  -- for late-arriving data guardrails
- source_partition_max_ts (TIMESTAMP)

Implementation details
- Views are defined in dbt-style models and materialized as views in the warehouse.
- We intentionally avoid per-request semantic views for now to keep query latency and access patterns sane; drilldowns beyond the supported dimensions should happen via the raw telemetry tables owned by Telemetry (with caution).
- Added explicit constraints in docs for high-cardinality dimensions:
  - runtime_config is restricted to a small enumerated set (baseline/batch_8/cache_on/...) and must be set by runtime
  - quantization_profile follows Applied ML naming/versioning (e.g., int8_kv_v2, fp8_w8a8_v1)

Testing / validation
- Added model tests for non-null keys, non-negative token counts, and basic sanity checks on denominators.
- Backtested 14 days across us-east/us-west/eu-west; compared semantic.unit_econ_daily totals vs the existing aggregation job output and got <0.3% variance (primarily from late event windows; see Known limitations).

Known limitations
- Late events: hourly view will show partial data within the last ~2 hours depending on ingestion lag. We surface data_completeness_ratio for callers to gate dashboards.
- Discounts/credits: currently sourced from billing hooks daily rollups; intraday discount attribution is not supported.

Follow-ups
- ENG-2914 will wire reconciliation checks to use these semantic views directly (instead of bespoke query logic).
- ENG-2915/ENG-2916 will update the dashboard API + UI to query semantic.* only.

References
- Linear: ENG-2910, ENG-2919
- ADR: Blended cost per 1M output tokens definition (ADR-0142)

Checklist
- [x] Stable column names documented
- [x] Join keys documented with examples
- [x] Legacy ad-hoc views marked deprecated
- [x] Tests added for key invariants
- [x] Verified sample tie-out vs aggregation job output

docs: add unit econ semantic layer join guide + dimension constraints
warehouse tests: non-null keys, non-negative tokens, denominator guardrails

conversation:
Logan Wright (review): Can we be explicit about grain and which dimensions are “supported” vs “best effort”? We’ve been burned by people grouping on runtime_config_id variants.
Caleb Johnson (author): Yep. Updated docs with an explicit Supported dimensions section and renamed runtime_config_id -> runtime_config with an enumerated set + NULL-safe behavior.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please align naming with the aggregation job output. Right now we have output_token_count in the job and output_tokens here.
Caleb Johnson (author): Renamed to output_tokens/input_tokens in both the view and docs; also added comments mapping legacy names -> new names.

Thomas Baird (review): Concern: driver view adds more columns and people will join it incorrectly, causing double counting. Can we provide examples?
Caleb Johnson (author): Added “safe join patterns” examples (join on dt/model_variant/region/customer_tier/runtime_config/quantization_profile) and a warning about joining driver_daily to daily without full keys.

Mei Lin (review): Tests: can we add a check that blended_cost_per_1m_output_tokens_usd is NULL when output_tokens=0 to avoid inf/NaN?
Caleb Johnson (author): Added a dbt test + updated expression to NULLIF(output_tokens,0).

Laura Bennett (comment via Logan): Finance needs to know what’s excluded. Please make sure credits/discounts are called out as included and sourced from billing rollups.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added a “Included/Excluded” section and a short note on the daily billing rollup dependency.

Final review
Logan Wright: Approved
Nadia Rahman: Approved
Thomas Baird: Approved
